label: nyiso 38 unified-ct-ramp (PROBE)
definition: (PROBE, NOT-YET) Keeper-34 migration onto the unified registry-driven reliability-floor engine, now with a new CONTINUOUS temperature-ramp family (inject_reliability_floor interpolates (threshold, floor_pct) knots) that faithfully reproduces the legacy downstate CT/ST floors' base+slope(T-T0) commitment curve instead of an over-firing step. Config = keeper-34 exact (offer curve, gas_hub_basis_daily+overlay, zonal gas basis, local-selfsupply/firm-imports/import-recon, energy-reserve co-opt). Still FAILS C1: 2024 ST_GAS -1.94 TWh (band +/-1.35), 2023 CC_REGULAR +2.61, 2023 ST_GAS -1.30. Root cause is NOT the floor mechanism (the floor forces the same energy) but an economic merit-order shift since keeper-34's unrecoverable dirty sha: Capital_Hudson ST (base_24h=0 in the data, so purely economic) is squeezed to 0.30 TWh vs ~1.2 in keeper 34. Closing it would need a CH persistent base ungrounded in data (rule #9/#11) or offer-curve residual-tuning (forbidden for a do-no-harm migration). The continuous-ramp engine stays as correct structure (rule #1) regardless of the fit.
